setups.name: LBNL xenon TPC + photon test cell
setups.institute: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL) / UC Berkeley
setups.location_note: 'LBNL Xenon Lab (formerly the TPC Lab)' on the LBNL site, 1 Cyclotron Rd, Berkeley (surface lab); approximate position (site level).
setups.medium: Xe (dual-phase TPC; also operated S1-only in liquid, and evacuated)
setups.years_active: 2017– (delayed-electron study published 2017/18; SiPM TPC test stand documented from 2022; delayed-photon campaign 2024–2025)
setups.description: Small liquid-xenon test stand at LBNL: a ~700 g dual-phase TPC (quoted as ~500 g in a 2025 talk) read out by 32 SiPM channels (Hamamatsu S13371; later 16 SiPMs + 1 PMT), with a typical single-electron size of ~24 phd; the same test stand hosted crystaLiZe, HydroX and SiPM R&D. Delayed single photons and electrons after ¹³³Ba Compton scatters are sampled out to ~5 ms with a 'cascade trigger' (the trigger window followed by further delayed 100 µs windows). For the 2025 paper the 3 cm diameter cell was run scintillation-only (no fields, ²¹⁰Po alpha source on a central grid, T = -99 C) with twelve 6 mm S13371 SiPM channels plus one LUX-type R8778 PMT; PTFE walls were swapped for Kapton and then aluminium, the cell was evacuated to use Cherenkov light in the PMT window as UV source, and a windowless S13370 SiPM was compared with a quartz-windowed S13371 in two optically isolated halves.

measurements.what: Delayed photon rate after S1 or S1+S2, written dp(t) = α·a·t^k, in TPC and S1-only configurations
measurements.result: Single power law out to 5 ms with -1.3 ≲ k ≲ -0.8 depending on event selection; insensitive to xenon purity and applied fields; α the same within 20% for S1-only and TPC

measurements.what: Systematic removal of suspect materials (PTFE → Kapton → aluminium; PMT ↔ SiPM; steel electrode removed; liquid level varied or surface removed)
measurements.result: No change in the power law other than total photon detection efficiency; suspects narrowed to the xenon or the photosensor (quartz window)

measurements.what: Delayed photons with vacuum in the cell, excited by Cherenkov pulses in the R8778 window (average 329 photons detected)
measurements.result: Power law persists without xenon: α = 2.22×10⁻³, k = -1.03 (10 µs to 1 ms)

measurements.what: Power-law parameters with liquid-xenon scintillation as excitation, 10 µs to 1 ms
measurements.result: S13371 SiPM: α = 2.30×10⁻³, k = -1.08 (also 0.399×10⁻³, k = -1.41 in the lower-rate configuration); R8778 PMT: α = 0.200×10⁻³, k = -1.31

measurements.what: Windowless S13370 SiPM versus quartz-windowed S13371 in optically isolated halves of the same cell
measurements.result: Delayed photon rate lower by a factor ~20 in the 50-100 µs bin without quartz; residual component with shallow slope (k = -0.238, α = 1.39) attributed tentatively to the ceramic package

measurements.what: Illustrative accidental-coincidence consequence (calculation in the paper, not a measurement)
measurements.result: A ×10 higher photon rate raises the 3-fold S1 accidental rate in a 200 ns window from 5.8 Hz to 5.8 kHz; 2-fold rates are ×250 higher

measurements.what: Effect of deliberately worse xenon purity on delayed electrons and photons (TPC mode)
measurements.result: Impurities increase the electron trains; photon trains unaffected (no number given on slides)

measurements.what: 235 nm LED flash (2 µs) added after a particle scatter
measurements.result: Delayed photon emission ~×5 and delayed electron emission ~×3 higher; LED alone gives photon trains but no electron trains

measurements.what: Interim interpretation of the delayed-photon source (later revised)
measurements.result: CPAD 2024 attributed delayed photons to metastable atomic xenon after the PTFE → Al swap left them unchanged, and reported ~×50 more delayed photons after gas scintillation than liquid; the 2025 paper instead identifies quartz window fluorescence as dominant

measurements.what: Earlier LBNL study of delayed single electrons after ionising events
measurements.result: Two components: a fast one reduced by increasing the field (compatible with electrons trapped at the liquid surface) and a slow one increasing linearly with field

setups.key_results: UV-induced fluorescence of the quartz photosensor windows is the dominant source of the power-law delayed photon noise at t < 5 ms (Phys. Rev. D 112, 052004): the noise survives removal of PTFE, of the steel grid, of the liquid surface and even of the xenon, and drops ~×20 with a windowless SiPM. In TPC mode (talks, 2024-2025) impurities raise electron trains but not photon trains, and a 235 nm LED flash after an event raises both, which the group reads as: electrons captured on impurities are released by the delayed photons. Whether quartz fluorescence still dominates at 5 ms to 1 s, the regime relevant for the underground experiments, is stated as open.
mechanisms: UV-induced fluorescence/phosphorescence of quartz (fused silica) photosensor windows
fluorescence of SiPM ceramic package (residual, tentative)
electron capture on electronegative impurities and release by delayed (fluorescence) photons (hypothesis)
PTFE fluorescence tested and found not dominant
electrons trapped at the liquid surface (fast component, 2017 study)

setups.name: LBNL PTFE fluorescence testbed
setups.institute: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL)
setups.location_note: Bench setup in the Sorensen xenon lab at LBNL; approximate position (site level).
setups.description: Small room-temperature test chamber built at LBNL as an undergraduate internship project to look for delayed light from detector materials. A sample (PTFE; PEEK and acrylic were also listed as candidates) is excited with an LED and the photons emitted at later times are counted with a silicon photomultiplier inside the chamber, compared against a control without the sample. It was meant to identify the main source of the 'photon trains' seen in the LBNL xenon TPC.

measurements.what: Photon counts versus time after LED excitation of PTFE, SiPM readout, ~300 K, vacuum
measurements.result: A distinct decay of photon counts at delayed times, 'suggestive of fluorescence'; a difference between PTFE and control is shown on slides; no rate or time constant published

setups.key_results: Delayed light after LED excitation was seen with PTFE in the chamber, but the abstract itself says an upgraded setup with lower systematics is needed to confirm that it comes from the PTFE. The same group later found in its xenon cell that replacing PTFE by aluminium leaves the delayed photons unchanged and that quartz photosensor windows dominate (Phys. Rev. D 112, 052004), so PTFE is not the main source there.
mechanisms: UV/LED-induced fluorescence of PTFE (impurities in PTFE)
fluorescence of other dielectrics (PEEK, acrylic) as candidates

setups.name: CrystaLiZe
setups.institute: University of Texas at Austin (Kravitz lab); prototype built and first operated at LBNL
setups.location_note: Current host: Department of Physics, UT Austin, 2515 Speedway (approximate position, physics building). The 700 g prototype results (2022-2023) were obtained at LBNL, Berkeley (37.876, -122.251).
setups.medium: solid Xe (crystalline xenon with xenon vapour above)
setups.years_active: 2022– (LBNL prototype papers 2022–2023; UT Austin affiliation from Dec 2023; kg-scale freezes at UT Austin reported 2025–2026)
setups.description: Dual-phase crystalline/vapour xenon TPC: the liquid below the surface is frozen into a transparent crystal (Bridgman-style growth with a ~1 K/cm gradient) while electrons are still extracted into the vapour and read out by electroluminescence. The LBNL prototype held 700 g and used 8 Hamamatsu VUV4 S13371 SiPMs (32 channels) on the shared LBNL TPC test stand. At UT Austin the group is scaling up in a larger cryostat with SiPMs and camera viewports (8 kg volume, most freezes at ~6 kg, 16 kg and 30 kg planned). The main goal is radon exclusion; the link to accidental coincidences and electron trains is an expectation, not a measurement.

measurements.what: First operation of a crystalline/vapour xenon TPC with electroluminescence readout
measurements.result: Works like a liquid/vapour TPC; scintillation yield in crystalline xenon appears identical to liquid

measurements.what: Radon ingress into the crystal, from the rate of radon-chain alphas versus time
measurements.result: More than a factor 500 exclusion of radon compared with the liquid state (alpha counts ~2000 in liquid vs 3 in crystal, as shown in the 2025 talk)

measurements.what: Expected effect on accidentals and electron trains (argument on slides, marked 'requires studies at UT to verify')
measurements.result: Up to ×2 shorter drift time → ~×2 fewer accidentals; better extraction efficiency → lower extraction field and less spurious emission; 'smaller electron-trains?' posed as a question

measurements.what: Scale-up freezes at UT Austin
measurements.result: Xe run 1: 3.5 days to freeze, visibly transparent; Xe run 2: 7.5 days, >90% VUV transparency (preliminary)

measurements.what: Status of the accidental / electron-train question in mid-2026
measurements.result: Still listed as not yet measured (verification at UT pending)

setups.key_results: Measured so far: stable operation of a 700 g crystalline/vapour TPC with liquid-like scintillation yield (JINST 2022) and >×500 radon exclusion (arXiv:2312.15082). The claims relevant to accidental coincidences - ~×2 shorter drift time, better electron extraction, possibly smaller electron trains - are arguments on conference slides; as of July 2026 no measurement of delayed electrons or accidentals in crystalline xenon has been shown.
mechanisms: electron trapping at the condensed-phase/vapour interface (expected to be reduced by better extraction)
spurious electrode emission (lower extraction field needed)
accidental pile-up scaling with maximum drift time

setups.name: Nikhef photoluminescence bench (VULCAN)
setups.institute: Nikhef Dark Matter Group / Institute of Physics, University of Amsterdam (Pollmann group); cryogenic part done with the TUM spectrofluorometer (A. Leonhardt)
setups.location_note: Nikhef, Science Park 105, Amsterdam; approximate position (building level). The temperature-dependent 310 nm measurements used the cryogenic spectrofluorometer at TUM (Garching).
setups.medium: vacuum (samples on a holder; ~10⁻⁵ mbar for the VUV scan at room temperature; 10⁻⁴ to 10⁻⁸ mbar on a cold finger, 87-293 K, for the 310 nm scan). No xenon in the bench.
setups.description: Ex-situ photoluminescence (PL) bench for detector materials and contaminants. VUV part: Hamamatsu L15094 H2D2 lamp, McPherson 234/302 monochromator (1200 g/mm Al+MgF2 grating), IdealVac sample chamber at ~10⁻⁵ mbar with a rotating three-sample copper holder viewed by six Hamamatsu S13360-6050CS SiPMs in photon-counting mode (sensitive 280-900 nm, 7% geometric acceptance); lamp spectrum used 120-200 nm, steady-state illumination, room temperature. Temperature part: 310 nm LED excitation of samples on a cold finger in vacuum, emission spectra 400-900 nm with an Ocean Optics QE65000 spectrometer at 87 K, 175 K and 293 K (setup of Leonhardt et al.). VULCAN (Vacuum Ultraviolet Light Characterization At Nikhef) is described as a tabletop experiment for reflectance, fluorescence spectra, fluorescence timing and wavelength-shifting measurements with single-photon sensitivity. The bench work is paired with an analysis of delayed lone hits in XENONnT data (Kharbanda).

measurements.what: PL of residue of two commercial solder fluxes (Stannol KS115, used in XENONnT; Chemtronics CW8400, used in LZ) under VUV excitation 120-200 nm at room temperature, relative to a PEN reference.
measurements.result: Both residues luminesce in the SiPM band (280-900 nm): average response relative to PEN 4.4% ± 0.8% (KS115) and 2.5% ± 0.6% (CW8400); no significant dependence on excitation wavelength; PL efficiencies of order 1%.

measurements.what: Emission spectra and integrated intensity (400-900 nm) of the two flux residues versus temperature under 310 nm excitation.
measurements.result: At LXe temperature (175 K) the PL efficiency is 2.40 ± 0.06 times (KS115) and 1.04 ± 0.02 times (CW8400) the room-temperature value; extrapolated to ~8% (KS115) and ~2% (CW8400) of PEN at LXe temperature.

measurements.what: Thermal-cycling observation: a KS115 solder point cooled to ~80 K.
measurements.result: Flux residue fragments into small photoluminescent flakes, a possible route for PL particulates to reach the active volume.

measurements.what: Side result on the photosensors: nominally VUV-blind Hamamatsu S13360 SiPMs exposed directly to the VUV beam.
measurements.result: The SiPM packaging itself photoluminesces; response rises above ~180 nm (treated as a systematic).

measurements.what: In-situ counterpart (XENONnT data): time profile of delayed lone hits after S2s, fitted over a 150 s window for hits >2.2 ms after the S2.
measurements.result: Power law with exponential cut-off: r_dc = 1.8 kHz, α = 0.065 PE/Hz, k = -0.65, τ = 0.28 s (slides, preliminary); lone-S1 rate 15 Hz and lone-S2 rate 150 mHz quoted.

measurements.what: In-situ counterpart (XENONnT data): top-array pattern of delayed lone hits compared with that of the preceding S2.
measurements.result: The ~7 brightest PMTs that receive 40% of the S2 light receive only 6% of the lone hits, so quartz-window PL is not the only mechanism.

measurements.what: EDX and LIBS composition analysis of particulates from, or representative of, the XENONnT TPC; temperature-dependent and time-resolved PL under 120-190 nm (LIDINE 2026 poster abstract).

setups.key_results: All tested solder-flux residues (the fluxes used in XENONnT and LZ) photoluminesce in the visible under VUV light, at a few per cent of PEN, i.e. PL efficiencies of order 1%, and for KS115 the yield rises 2.4-fold at LXe temperature. Flux residue flakes off on cooling. In XENONnT data the delayed lone hits follow a power law with a ~0.3 s cut-off and are only weakly correlated with the S2 hit pattern, which argues against PMT quartz fluorescence as the sole source. No PL time constants have been published yet.
mechanisms: photoluminescence of solder-flux residue (rosin/resin, PAH-forming) under xenon/argon VUV scintillation
PL of particulates and surface contaminants reaching the active volume
delayed photons as a source of lone hits / lone S1 pile-up
photoionisation of impurities by delayed PL photons (hypothesis, delayed electrons)

references.title: Photoluminescence of resin-based solder flux residue under ultraviolet excitation from 120 nm to 310 nm
Investigation of photoluminescence as a source of instrumental backgrounds in xenon TPCs (slides titled 'Delayed Photon backgrounds in XENONnT experiment')
Optical characterization of detector materials using VULCAN
LIDINE 2026 poster (contribution 72) on detector materials, contaminants and xenon impurities as sources of delayed signals; EDX/LIBS of XENONnT-like particulates; PL under 120-190 nm
A novel cryogenic VUV spectrofluorometer for the characterization of wavelength shifters

caveats: The poster results (EDX/LIBS composition, time-resolved photoluminescence) are announced in an abstract only; no numbers are public.
The XENONnT numbers come from conference slides and are preliminary, not from a collaboration paper.
Identification of the VUV monochromator setup of the flux-residue paper with VULCAN at Nikhef rests on the LIDINE 2026 talk; the paper does not state it.
No photoluminescence time constants have been published.

setups.name: TUM VUV photoluminescence setup
setups.institute: Physik-Department E15, Technische Universität München
setups.location_note: Physik-Department, James-Franck-Str., 85748 Garching bei München; approximate position (TUM Garching campus).
setups.years_active: 2019 (single published campaign)
setups.description: Room-temperature VUV fluorescence bench: Cathodeon deuterium lamp with MgF2 window, VM-502 vacuum monochromator (1200 lines/mm grating, ~20 nm FWHM at the slit widths used), sample tube sealed to the monochromator at below 5.4×10⁻⁴ mbar. Emitted light is collected by a quartz lens and fibre and read either by an Ocean Optics QE65000 spectrometer or by a photon-counting PMT (S20 cathode, MgF2 window). Excitation 130-250 nm, emission window 400-550 nm, signal integrated over minutes; efficiency normalised to an evaporated TPB film measured under the same conditions. Sensitive to low-intensity steady-state PL but not to its time structure.

measurements.what: Search for visible (400-550 nm) photoluminescence of the LUX PTFE batch and two DEAP-3600 acrylic (PMMA) batches under 130-250 nm excitation at room temperature.
measurements.result: No PL signal; upper limits on the wavelength-shifting efficiency of 0.05% to 0.35% of that of TPB.

setups.key_results: No photoluminescence was found from the specific PTFE (LUX) and acrylic (DEAP-3600) batches; the wavelength-shifting efficiency is below 0.05-0.35% of TPB for 130-250 nm excitation and 400-550 nm emission. The measurement is steady-state, at room temperature, and limited to that emission window, so slow or cold-enhanced PL and emission outside 400-550 nm are not excluded.
mechanisms: photoluminescence / fluorescence of bulk PTFE and acrylic under VUV (negative result)

references.title: Photoluminescence response of acrylic (PMMA) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) to ultraviolet light

caveats: The measurement is steady-state, at room temperature and limited to 400–550 nm emission; slow or cold-enhanced photoluminescence and emission outside that window are not excluded.
Coordinates are approximate (campus level).

setups.name: ASTERiX
setups.institute: Purdue University, Department of Physics and Astronomy
setups.collaboration: LBECA (Purdue, LLNL, UCSD, LBNL, Stony Brook)
setups.location_note: Surface laboratory of the Lang group at Purdue University; approximate position (physics building).
setups.years_active: study published 2021 (data-taking dates not stated)
setups.description: ASTERiX ('A Small TPC for Experimental Research in Xenon') is a ~150 g dual-phase xenon TPC: a PTFE cylinder 7.5 cm in diameter with a 1 cm drift region, three etched meshes 1 cm apart, the liquid level held 2.5 mm above the gate by a weir, and seven 1-inch Hamamatsu R8520 PMTs in a top array only. Nominal fields were 500 V/cm drift and 5.9 kV/cm extraction in the liquid (11 kV/cm in the gas). Event windows of just over 5 ms after 122 keV ⁵⁷Co Compton interactions were recorded, with a maximum drift time of only ~10 µs, so that delayed single- and few-electron signals could be followed in time and (x,y), and an optical fibre delivered up to 1 W of 1550 nm infrared light into the target.

measurements.what: Rate of position-correlated single-electron signals versus time after the primary S2 (fit 30 µs to 1 ms)
measurements.result: Power law R = A·t^b with b = -1.20 ± 0.04 (stat); 80% of the position-correlated single electrons lie within 9.9 mm of the primary

measurements.what: Dependence on extraction field (5.9, 5.3, 4.7, 4.1, 3.5 kV/cm in the liquid)
measurements.result: Amplitude rises linearly with extraction field while the exponent does not change; slopes (97 ± 2)×10⁻⁵, (47 ± 3)×10⁻⁵ and (23 ± 1)×10⁻⁵ per kV/cm for the three electron-multiplicity classes

measurements.what: Dependence on drift field (100 to 1000 V/cm) and on interaction depth
measurements.result: Single-electron rate increases with drift field; normalised to the primary S2, rates increase linearly with depth

measurements.what: Illumination with 1 W of 1550 nm (0.8 eV) infrared light to test photodetachment from impurities
measurements.result: No reduction of the single- and few-electron backgrounds

setups.key_results: Delayed single- and few-electron rates after a ⁵⁷Co interaction follow a power law in time (b = -1.20 ± 0.04 between 30 µs and 1 ms), are position-correlated with the parent S2, grow linearly with extraction field and with interaction depth, and increase with drift field. One watt of 1550 nm light does not reduce them. The thesis concludes that these backgrounds originate at the liquid-gas interface, while the depth dependence is also what an impurity mechanism predicts.
mechanisms: delayed emission of electrons trapped at the liquid-gas interface
electron capture on impurities and later release (depth dependence)
photodetachment by infrared light tested, no effect

setups.name: UCSD sealed TPC
setups.institute: University of California San Diego, Department of Physics
setups.collaboration: LBECA (Purdue, LLNL, UCSD, LBNL, Stony Brook)
setups.location_note: Surface laboratory of the Ni group at UC San Diego, La Jolla; approximate position (physics department).
setups.years_active: c. 2020 (preprint July 2020, published January 2021)
setups.description: Dual-phase xenon TPC whose target is sealed off from the rest of the detector vessel: an acrylic cylinder (63 mm diameter × 59 mm high, 0.54 kg of the 1.13 kg of xenon) closed at top and bottom by fused-silica windows on Teflon O-rings, so that the outgassing materials outside do not feed impurities into the drift volume. The bottom window carries a single-layer graphene coating that serves as the cathode (~96% transparency); gate, anode and top screen are etched stainless-steel meshes, and four 1-inch R8520 PMTs view the target through the top window. Purity was followed with a ⁵⁷Co source while single electrons produced within one drift time of an S2 were counted separately for the gate, the cathode and the liquid bulk.

measurements.what: Electron lifetime and outgassing in the sealed volume
measurements.result: Best electron lifetime (456 ± 96) µs ('a little over 0.5 ms'); effective impurity outgassing rate (4.0 ± 0.3)×10⁻¹¹ l/s from a purification model

measurements.what: Single-electron gain from photoionisation electrons at gate and cathode
measurements.result: 4.7 ± 2.3 PE/e⁻ (gate) and 4.3 ± 1.8 PE/e⁻ (cathode) at 5.4 kV/cm extraction field in the liquid

measurements.what: Prompt (within one drift time) single-electron rate from the liquid bulk versus purity
measurements.result: Decreases as the electron lifetime improves and scales linearly with the impurity concentration; rates from gate and cathode are much less affected

measurements.what: Photo-electron emission of the graphene-coated cathode compared with stainless steel
measurements.result: Comparison reported in the paper; no number quoted here.

setups.key_results: The sealed design reaches sub-millisecond electron lifetime in a 0.54 kg target, and the rate of single electrons produced in the liquid bulk by S2 light falls linearly with the impurity concentration, as expected for photoionisation of neutral impurities. The study covers only the prompt single electrons within a drift time; the paper states that delayed single-electron emission was left for future work.
mechanisms: photoionisation of impurities in the liquid bulk by S2 light
photoelectric emission from gate and cathode (graphene vs stainless steel)
impurity supply by outgassing of detector materials

setups.name: UCSD LXePSC (radial single-phase)
setups.institute: University of California San Diego, Department of Physics
setups.location_note: Surface laboratory of the Ni group at UC San Diego, La Jolla; approximate position (physics department).
setups.years_active: 2021–2024 (three runs: radial TPC 2021, 10 µm wire run 2023, higher-gain run 2024)
setups.description: Single-phase liquid xenon proportional scintillation counter (formerly 'radial TPC'): a cylindrical target with a thin gold-plated tungsten anode wire on the axis (25, 10 and 17.8 µm diameter in successive runs) and twenty cathode wires 2.5 cm away, so electrons drift radially and produce electroluminescence in the liquid at the wire surface. Eight 1-inch R8520 PMTs (four in a top row, four in a bottom row) surround the 12 cm high barrel; the maximum drift time is ~15 µs. There is no liquid-gas interface, which makes it a control experiment for the hypothesis that electron trains come from electrons trapped at the surface.

measurements.what: Electroluminescence gain in liquid with a 10 µm anode wire at 3.6 kV
measurements.result: g2 = 1.6 ± 0.2 PE/e⁻, i.e. 17 ± 4 photons per electron; single electrons from cathode photoemission at 1.8 PE/e⁻

measurements.what: Delayed signals 30-600 µs after S2 in the 2023 run
measurements.result: Lone-hit rate follows a power law plus constant with exponent -1.16 (vs -0.7 in XENON1T); two-PMT coincidences are consistent with lone-hit pile-up, i.e. no significant single-electron contribution

measurements.what: Electron trains in the higher-gain run (17.8 µm wire, 3-fold PMT coincidence, g2 ~ 3.3 PE/e⁻ from simulation fit)
measurements.result: A single-electron component that scales with the primary S2 area and decays over several ms as a power law with exponents -1.07 and -1.05 (two fitted selections), similar to dual-phase TPCs, plus a constant background from spurious light emission

setups.key_results: The first analysis (JINST 2023) saw delayed signals dominated by single-photon-like hits with no evidence of electron trains, but at a gain of only 1.6 PE/e⁻ single electrons could not be separated from photons. With higher gain the follow-up (Phys. Rev. D 111, 012005) does observe a power-law single-electron train (exponent about -1.05 to -1.07) without any liquid-gas interface, and concludes that removing the interface alone is unlikely to reduce the electron-train background.
mechanisms: electrons trapped at the liquid-gas interface (tested by removing the interface; trains persist)
capture on and release from impurities in the bulk (favoured by the follow-up)
photoemission from cathode wires within one drift time
spurious light emission at the high-field anode wire

setups.years_active: 2018– (TUNL run 2018; extraction paper 2019; hardware upgrades reported in a 2024 thesis)
setups.description: XeNu (spelled XeNeu in later LLNL work) is a prototype dual-phase xenon TPC optimised for low-energy ionisation signals: about 140 g of liquid xenon in a cylindrical active volume between etched stainless-steel grids, viewed by four Hamamatsu R8520-406 PMTs above and one R8778 PMT in the liquid below. It reached extraction fields up to 10.4 kV/cm in the liquid, the highest reported at the time, and triggers on single electrons with ~100% efficiency. Later upgrades replaced the PTFE/PEEK parts with low-outgassing metal and machinable ceramic and the PMT array with S13371 SiPMs, specifically to study electron trains. LBECA is the related proposal for a 100 kg-scale low-background electron-counting detector.

measurements.result: Apparent saturation between 7.5 and 10.4 kV/cm in the liquid, where the efficiency is stable at the 1% per kV/cm level; taken as indication that ~100% extraction is approached

A 2024 thesis reports preliminary evidence that removing plastics from XeNeu reduces electron trains.

instabilities of the charged liquid surface producing e-bursts (hypothesis)

setups.name: Imperial College wire-emission chamber
setups.institute: High Energy Physics Group, Blackett Laboratory, Imperial College London
setups.location_note: Blackett Laboratory, Imperial College London, SW7 2AZ (approximate position).
setups.years_active: ca. 2014–2018 (paper 2018; exact start year not stated in the paper)
setups.description: Small (4 kg) two-phase xenon chamber with single-electron sensitivity in which one cathodic wire sample is stretched below a 60 mm wide gate/anode grid pair; a single 2-inch quartz-windowed ETEL D730/9829Q PMT in the gas phase views the electroluminescence region. The wire voltage is ramped slowly (1 V/s) while 250 µs waveforms are recorded, so emitted electrons are counted individually and emission currents down to 10⁻¹⁸ A are detectable. Wires of 40-200 µm diameter and several alloys (LUX gate and cathode wire, ZEPLIN-III SS316L, BeCu) were tested up to surface fields of several hundred kV/cm, before and after electropolishing or nitric-acid cleaning and passivation. The work was part of the LZ grid R&D.

measurements.what: Voltage-ramp tests of single cathodic wires in two-phase xenon with electron counting.
measurements.result: Emission episodes at surface fields as low as ~10 kV/cm in some wires; average rates 10-200 counts/s with outbreaks up to ~10⁶ counts/s; a fainter, steadier emission in all untreated samples; sensitivity to currents of 10⁻¹⁸ A.

measurements.what: Search for an intrinsic emission threshold at the metal-LXe interface.
measurements.result: None found up to at least 160 kV/cm; phenomenology inconsistent with field emission from microscopic filaments; partial conditioning on repeated ramps.

measurements.what: Effect of surface treatment: ultrasonic cleaning in 35% HNO3 at 45 C for 30 min followed by passivation in deionised water (LUX cathode wire samples); electropolishing.
measurements.result: Nitric-acid cleaning and passivation: at least an order of magnitude lower overall emission; over four runs no extended emitters and a single double-candidate waveform (at 53 kV/cm). Electropolishing helps less.

setups.key_results: Spurious electron emission from cathodic wires in LXe starts at fields as low as ~10 kV/cm, far below field-emission expectations, and is tied to the surface quality (corrosion, oxide layer) rather than to microscopic protrusions. Cleaning stainless-steel wire with nitric acid and passivating it reduces the emission by at least an order of magnitude. No intrinsic threshold exists up to at least 160 kV/cm.
mechanisms: spurious electron emission from cathodic (gate/cathode) wires
surface oxide / corrosion-related emission rather than Fowler-Nordheim field emission

setups.description: The 'LZ System Test' at SLAC was a suite of three detectors with single-electron sensitivity built to qualify the LZ grids. The Gas Test held small prototype grid pairs (14-20 cm) in room-temperature xenon gas at a pressure chosen to match the cold-gas density in LZ, viewed by two PMTs. Phase 1 was a ~30 kg dual-phase TPC cloning the LZ extraction region, with a 32-PMT top array, 6 skin PMTs and one bottom PMT. Phase 2 held the full-size 1.5 m LZ extraction region in 3.3 bar xenon gas under a sparse array of 32 PMTs in an Al/MgF2 reflective box (~1% light collection), giving coarse (x,y) localisation of emission. Electrons emitted from the cathodic grid are detected one by one through their electroluminescence.

measurements.what: Electron emission from a stainless-steel grid in gas, measured by proportional scintillation, versus field
measurements.result: Consistent with Fowler-Nordheim emission with field-enhancement parameter β = 1988 after electropolishing

measurements.what: Sensitivity of the gas-phase technique and effect of acid passivation
measurements.result: Emission currents down to the atto-ampere level measurable; citric-acid passivation reduces electron emission from stainless steel

measurements.what: 20 cm grid before and after passivation (maximum surface field 117 kV/cm)
measurements.result: Two reproducible emission hot spots on the untreated grid are gone after passivation; chromium-oxide layer thickens from ~30 Å to ~70 Å (preliminary)

measurements.what: Full-scale LZ extraction region in gas (Phase 2), gate-anode voltage stepped to 12 kV
measurements.result: Localised hot spots of single-electron-like pulses, some bins above 100 Hz, that appear or disappear when dust is added or removed between runs; one persistent spot attributed to a wire defect; breakdown at 10 kV, stable at 11 kV

measurements.what: Point-like emitter and 'training' in Phase 1 / Phase 2 prototype grids
measurements.result: Emitter turning on near 10.5 kV gate-anode voltage and removed by a spark; holding the grid at voltage for hours lowers emission by a factor ~2 (preliminary)

measurements.what: Single electrons and single photoelectrons after large S2s in the Phase 1 dual-phase TPC (12.5 kV)
measurements.result: Both rates are high after pulses >10⁵-10⁶ phe and decay over tens of ms; attributed to incomplete extraction plus photoionisation of impurities (electrons) and to Teflon fluorescence (photons) - preliminary, no numbers

setups.key_results: The SLAC group showed that grid electron emission can be measured in xenon gas with single-electron (atto-ampere) sensitivity and position resolution. Emission is concentrated in hot spots: permanent ones linked to wire defects, removed by citric-acid passivation, and transient ones linked to dust; an electropolished grid follows a Fowler-Nordheim law with β = 1988. These tests led to passivating the LZ gate grid and spray-washing all grids before installation.
mechanisms: field emission from wire defects / sharp points (Fowler-Nordheim with large field enhancement)
transient emission from dust and debris on the wires
surface oxide chemistry (passivation leaves a Cr-rich oxide)
delayed single electrons and photons after large S2s seen in Phase 1 (incomplete extraction, photoionisation, Teflon fluorescence - hypotheses)

setups.institute: Max-Planck-Institut für Kernphysik (MPIK), Heidelberg
setups.location_note: MPIK, Saupfercheckweg 1, 69117 Heidelberg (approximate position).
setups.years_active: ca. 2019– (TPC described in a 2022 paper; UV+IR configuration published 2025)
setups.description: Small dual-phase xenon TPC with a ~350 g liquid target, 5 cm drift between cathode and gate, PTFE wall, gate-anode gap 5 mm. In the 2025 configuration the top PMT is a 2-inch infrared-sensitive Hamamatsu R5509-73 behind an 8 mm aperture and the bottom PMT a UV-sensitive R6041-406, giving wavelength coverage 170-1700 nm. Drift field ~400 V/cm (max drift time ~30 µs), amplification field ~12 kV/cm in the gas (scanned 9-15 kV/cm), operation at about -95 C and 2.5 bar; alpha source (²²²Rn) signals. Having UV and IR channels on the same S1 and S2 lets delayed light be separated from delayed electrons, since delayed electrons must appear in the UV channel too.

measurements.what: Average S2 pulse shape in the UV channel (500 S2s).
measurements.result: Main peak Gaussian with σ ~0.2 µs, asymmetric late tail (PMT afterpulses and delayed electrons from incomplete extraction or impurity photoionisation), and a small peak ~1.5 µs after the main signal attributed to photoemission from the gate by S2 light (it depends on the amplification field; a similar delayed peak follows large S1s).

measurements.what: Time response of the IR channel after S1 and S2.
measurements.result: A slow component with ~30 µs time constant carrying about half (>50% after S2) of the IR signal, similar after S1 and S2; the IR tail after S2 is about an order of magnitude larger in relative amplitude than the UV tail and shows no gate-photoemission peak.

measurements.what: Dependence of the IR signal on the gas amplification field, 9-15 kV/cm.
measurements.result: Supports IR emission from electroluminescence.

setups.key_results: The UV S2 waveform shows a gate-photoemission peak ~1.5 µs after the S2 and a delayed-electron tail. The IR channel shows an unexplained ~30 µs component after both S1 and S2; the authors list a slow IR scintillation process, PTFE (or residue-in-PTFE) fluorescence, quartz-window fluorescence and a PMT effect as candidates, delayed electrons being excluded as the cause because they would also show in the UV channel. Runs at higher purity and at longer time scales are announced.
mechanisms: photoelectric emission from the gate electrode by S2 (and S1) light
delayed electrons from incomplete extraction or photoionisation of impurities
material fluorescence (PTFE, quartz PMT window) as an open explanation of a ~30 µs IR tail
infrared scintillation / electroluminescence of xenon

setups.name: Tsinghua prototype TPC (RELICS prototype)
setups.institute: Department of Physics & Center for High Energy Physics, Tsinghua University
setups.location_note: Tsinghua University campus, Beijing; approximate position (the papers give the institute address only). The full RELICS detector is planned for the Sanmen nuclear power plant, Zhejiang.
setups.description: Surface-level dual-phase xenon TPC prototype of the RELICS reactor-CEvNS experiment: cylindrical active volume 80 mm in diameter and 36 mm high (~0.55 kg LXe) inside PTFE walls, read out by Hamamatsu R8520-406 1-inch PMTs in top and bottom arrays (14 channels in total). Drift field ~180 V/cm (cathode at -3248 V), extraction field ~4 kV/cm in the liquid, single-electron gain 34.30 ± 0.01 PE/e⁻. Operated without passive shielding, so cosmic muons (~1 Hz) and gammas (~100 Hz) produce a dense delayed-electron (DE) background, which makes it a test bed for DE phenomenology and for veto strategies. The LIDINE 2025 poster by Y. Zhao reports studies of material optical properties, xenon purity and field effects on delayed photons and delayed electrons and an optimised prototype design.

measurements.what: S2-only event rate in the CEvNS region of interest of the prototype, before and after a high-energy veto (T_veto = 20 × Area_HE + 1.7×10⁶ ns), rise-time and fiducial cuts.
measurements.result: 3.77×10⁷ events/(kg day) before selection, 8.57×10³ events/(kg day) after; still about four orders of magnitude above the expected CEvNS rate of 0.98 events/(kg day). DE rate follows a power law in the time since the previous high-energy event.

measurements.what: Low-energy response with internal ³⁷Ar and ⁸³ᵐKr sources.
measurements.result: ³⁷Ar L-shell (0.27 keV) and K-shell (2.8 keV) peaks resolved in S2-only analysis after the DE veto; single-electron gain 34.30 ± 0.01 (stat.) PE/e⁻.

measurements.what: Delayed-electron phenomenology in RELICS prototype data (TAUP 2025 poster).
measurements.result: DEs correlated in time and position with preceding high-energy events; drift time, xenon purity and extraction field affect DE emission; a correlation-based selection reduces the background in the CEvNS region by 1 to 2 orders of magnitude.

measurements.what: Origins of delayed photons and delayed electrons: material optical properties, xenon purity and electric-field effects; test of an optimised prototype (LIDINE 2025 poster).

setups.key_results: In the unshielded prototype the delayed-electron background after muons and gammas dominates the sub-keV S2-only region: vetoes bring it from 3.8×10⁷ to 8.6×10³ events/(kg day), still ~10⁴ times the CEvNS signal. DEs are correlated in time (power law) and position with earlier high-energy events and depend on drift time, purity and extraction field. The 0.27 keV ³⁷Ar line is nevertheless resolved. No quantitative result on delayed photons or on material optics has been published.

delayed photons linked to material optical properties
extraction/drift field dependence of delayed emission
pile-up of delayed electrons mimicking few-electron S2s

setups.name: RED-100 electron shutter (double gate) / RED-1
setups.institute: National Research Nuclear University MEPhI (Moscow Engineering Physics Institute), with NRC Kurchatov Institute - ITEP
setups.location_note: Ground-level laboratory at NRNU MEPhI, Kashirskoe shosse 31, Moscow 115409 (approximate position), where RED-1 and the 2019 RED-100 test ran. RED-100 was then operated in 2021-2022 at 19 m from the core of a Kalinin Nuclear Power Plant reactor (Udomlya, Tver region).
setups.years_active: RED-1: results 2012–2016; RED-100: lab test Feb 2019, KNPP run 2021–2022; argon refill tests announced in 2024
setups.description: RED-100 is a two-phase xenon emission detector for reactor CEvNS: ~200 kg of LXe in a titanium cryostat, 160 kg in the drift volume (later quoted as 126 kg; sensitive volume 36 cm diameter × 41.5 cm), PTFE dodecagon reflector, two arrays of nineteen 3-inch Hamamatsu R11410-20 PMTs. Its patented 'electron shutter' is an extra grid G1 placed 3 mm below the extraction grid G2 (hexagonal etched stainless-steel meshes, 4 mm cells): when an S1 above threshold (a muon) is seen, a +300 V pulse on G1, typically 1 ms long, closes the shutter so that the ionisation electrons of that event do not reach the liquid surface; the PMTs are gated off by the same pulse. This is the 'double gate' of the Pereverzev review; it separates single-electron noise born at the surface (electrons trapped under the liquid surface) from noise born below the shutter. RED-1 is the group's earlier small two-phase xenon chamber in which delayed electron emission and delayed electroluminescence after muons were studied.

measurements.what: Rate of 'spontaneous' single-electron (SE) signals in RED-100 in the ground-level MEPhI laboratory, without shielding, with the shutter operating (1 ms closure after muon S1s).
measurements.result: ~250 kHz with the shutter on; about a factor 3 higher with the shutter off. No strong correlation of the SE rate with xenon purity.

measurements.what: Consequences for CEvNS: accidental coincidences of SEs as the instrumental background to multi-electron events.
measurements.result: Threshold of 4 ionisation electrons judged feasible at KNPP assuming 50 kHz SE rate (250 kHz / 5 for the lower muon flux) and a point-likeness cut (r = 0.4, 60% CEvNS acceptance).

measurements.what: RED-1: delayed electroluminescence and spontaneous SE signals after cosmic muons.
measurements.result: SE rate strongly dependent on the time since the primary electroluminescence; both attributed to ionisation electrons trapped under the liquid-gas potential barrier.

measurements.what: Double-gate test as summarised by Pereverzev: closing potential applied for 1 ms after a large S1.
measurements.result: More than 95% of the primary ionisation electrons kept from the surface; SE rate ~250 kHz versus ~750 kHz when the 1 ms was merely vetoed; SEs reappear after reopening with a delay equal to the drift time from the second gate to the surface and no excess at switching, so most remaining emission originates below the grids (bulk liquid, cathode).

measurements.what: SE rate of RED-100 at the Kalinin NPP (shutter duration 0.3-6 ms depending on the event).
measurements.result: About an order of magnitude lower than at MEPhI, 25 kHz; SE flow non-Poissonian and spatially correlated, which undermines the point-likeness cut; only an upper limit on CEvNS (331 kg day reactor-on, 106 kg day reactor-off).

setups.key_results: Blocking the charge of muon events with a second grid 3 mm under the extraction grid lowers the single-electron rate by only a factor ~3 (to ~250 kHz at ground level): the surface-trapped component is removed, but most of the delayed single electrons come from the liquid volume or the cathode. The remaining SE flow is correlated in time and space, and its accidental pile-up set the limit of the RED-100 reactor run at Kalinin NPP (25 kHz SE rate, no CEvNS observation).
mechanisms: electrons trapped under the liquid-gas interface and emitted late (suppressed by the shutter)
delayed single electrons originating in the bulk liquid (impurity capture and release) or at the cathode
muon-induced electron trains; non-Poissonian, spatially correlated SE noise
accidental coincidence of single electrons faking few-electron events

setups.name: LZ few-electron study
setups.institute: Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF), Davis Cavern, 4850 ft level
setups.location_note: LZ detector underground in the Davis Cavern at SURF (4850 ft level, 4300 m w.e.); approximate position (SURF site).
setups.years_active: 2021– (commissioning, grid-tuning and WS2022 data analysed; paper 2025/2026)
setups.description: In-situ study in the LZ dual-phase xenon TPC (7 t active liquid xenon, 494 R11410-22 PMTs in two arrays, four high-voltage grids). It uses randomly triggered commissioning data, an 'extraction-region-only' configuration (gate -4 kV, anode +4 kV, cathode at 0 V) that isolates grid emission, and WS2022 data with electron lifetimes of 2-8 ms. The large cross-section and good single-electron position resolution (about 3 cm) allow position-correlated and position-uncorrelated electron rates to be separated from 3 ms to 1 s after a progenitor S2. Drift field 193 V/cm (also 110 and 240 V/cm); extraction fields 3410-4300 V/cm; the roughly 1 cm of liquid above the gate gives an in-situ test at 3.4-3.9 kV/cm.

measurements.what: Time dependence of position-correlated single-electron rate after S2s of at least 200 extracted electrons, fitted with a power law α·Δt^β between 3 and 200 ms (uncorrelated rate subtracted)
measurements.result: β = -1.13 ± 0.01 (stat), with a 10% systematic, at 193 V/cm; -1.04 at 110 V/cm and -1.01 at 240 V/cm (consistent within the systematic)

measurements.what: Power-law exponent for progenitors in the high-field liquid above the gate (fit range 3-20 ms)
measurements.result: β = -1.28 ± 0.29 at 3.4 kV/cm and -1.10 ± 0.29 at 3.9 kV/cm, i.e. no strong field dependence

measurements.what: Dependence on extraction field at fixed drift field
measurements.result: Exponent unchanged for extraction fields of 3410, 3900 and 4300 V/cm (extraction efficiency 50-78%)

measurements.what: Dependence on progenitor drift time and electron lifetime (2-8 ms)
measurements.result: Amplitude rises linearly with progenitor drift time, exponent does not; normalising to the number of electrons lost along the drift removes nearly all differences. At 5 ms lifetime the position-correlated electrons detected between 3 ms and 1 s are about 1.1% of the progenitor for 0.85 ms drift and about 0.3% for 0.3 ms drift, while 16% and 6% of the progenitor electrons are captured in those two cases

measurements.what: Position-uncorrelated electrons just after the maximum drift time
measurements.result: Rate falls quickly in the first 2-3 ms, explained as a photoionisation cascade (electroluminescence of extracted electrons photoionising again); after 3 ms pulses are almost only single electrons

measurements.what: Photon emitted in coincidence with electron emission from the gate (extraction-region-only data, hot spots visible in x-y)
measurements.result: Single photoelectrons precede small S2s by 2246.1 ± 0.3 ns, the gate-to-surface drift time

measurements.what: Rejection of grid emission with the gate-photon tag in WS2022 data (veto of the 4.5 ms event window)
measurements.result: S2 rate in the 2-4 electron region suppressed by more than an order of magnitude and single electrons by more than a factor 2; 93.60 ± 0.26% of S2-only events of 10-50 electrons are kept

measurements.what: Companion model of radon-daughter decays on cathode and gate wires as a source of small S2s with suppressed S1 (LZ and LUX data)
measurements.result: First-principles response model compared with LZ and LUX data; no single headline number.

setups.key_results: Delayed single electrons follow a power law close to t^-1 (β = -1.13 at the nominal field) that is insensitive to drift field, extraction field and purity, while the amplitude scales with the electrons lost to impurities during the drift: capture on bulk impurities and later release is the main origin, and unextracted electrons under the surface are subdominant (their contribution would fall, not rise, with drift time). The species responsible is only a subdominant part of the electronegative impurities. Spontaneous gate emission from hot spots is accompanied by a photon 2.25 µs earlier and can be vetoed with that tag at about 94% acceptance.
mechanisms: capture of drift electrons on bulk impurities and delayed release (power law ~t^-1)
unextracted electrons under the liquid surface (tested, subdominant)
spontaneous (hot-spot) electron emission from the gate grid, tagged by a coincident photon
photoionisation of impurities and photoelectric effect on metal within a drift time, plus a photoionisation cascade for 2-3 ms
radon-daughter decays on grid wires (companion paper)

setups.description: In-situ photon-level analysis of isolated S1 pulses in LZ (7 t active xenon, 494 3-inch R11410-22 PMTs). Small S1s have no usable position reconstruction, so the method uses the double-photoelectron (DPE) effect: a VUV photon has about a 20% chance of giving two photoelectrons in these PMTs, while longer-wavelength light does not, so the mean single-photon response separates xenon scintillation from non-VUV light. Tritiated methane (VUV) and blue LED (non-VUV) data calibrate the response for each PMT-coincidence level, and the single-photon rate after large S2s and muons is followed in time.

Photon make-up of isolated S1s from the DPE response
measurements.result: Most isolated S1s agree with the VUV calibration; at 3-fold there is clear non-VUV contamination: about 48% of 3-fold S1s come from pile-up of non-VUV single photons outside vetoed periods, against about 1% of 4-fold S1s

measurements.result: Power law, rate ~ t^b + c with b = -0.83 ± 0.07 and c = 4 ± 2 Hz

setups.name: LZ accidental-coincidence model
setups.institute: Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF), Davis Cavern, 4850 ft level
setups.location_note: LZ detector in the Davis Cavern at SURF; approximate position (SURF site). The model is built from LZ science data.
setups.years_active: 2022– (WS2022 'ChopStitch' model; environment-matched version for WS2025, data March 2023 – April 2025)
setups.description: Data-driven model of accidental S1-S2 pairs in LZ. Real isolated S1 and isolated S2 waveforms are chopped and stitched into synthetic single-scatter events ('Accidental ChopStitch'), and the rate is normalised to events with unphysical drift time (UDT, beyond the cathode: >951 µs in WS2022, >1100 µs in WS2024), which are pure accidentals. For the 2025 low-mass and ⁸B search (S1 2-15 photons detected, S2 3.5-14.5 electrons) pairs are drawn from the same single-photon and single-electron rate environment ('environment-matched pairing'), because both rates rise together and decay over seconds after large S2s, so small pile-up S1s preferentially meet small pile-up S2s. No physical mechanism is modelled individually: every source of isolated pulses enters through the measured pulses.

measurements.what: Accidental expectation, WS2022 (first science run) WIMP search with the ChopStitch model normalised to UDT events
measurements.result: 1.2 ± 0.3 events; shape cuts remove 99.6% of synthetic accidentals (>99.5% quoted in the results paper)

measurements.what: Accidental expectation, WS2024 (4.2 tonne-years)
measurements.result: 2.8 ± 0.6 events (fit 2.6 ± 0.6); cut rejection 99.5% on the UDT sideband (>1100 µs)

measurements.what: Accidental expectation, WS2025 low-mass + ⁸B search (5.7 tonne-years), after all cuts
measurements.result: 6.6 ± 0.3 events out of 19 observed; total expectation 27.2 (+10.1/-7.3)

measurements.what: Same number as given in the IOP 2026 talk, with its exposure-normalised form and background fractions
measurements.result: 6.55 ± 0.29 events (1.15 per tonne-year); about 3 times more accidentals than ⁸B events before pulse-based cuts; final sample about 30% accidentals, about 70% ⁸B, below 0.5% neutrons; in WS2024 accidentals were 0.2% of final events

measurements.what: Probability that an isolated S2 forms an accidental event as a function of the ambient single-photon and single-electron rates
measurements.result: 0.4% in normal conditions, approaching 100% at high rates

measurements.what: Validation on UDT events in the region of interest
measurements.result: Model 130.6 ± 1.4 (sys.) vs 139 observed; S1, S2 and 2D goodness-of-fit p-values 0.38, 0.48 and 0.28 (2D test: 4×4 equiprobable bins, 7.9 events expected per bin); normalisation-region p-values 0.72 (S1) and 0.59 (S2), agreement down to 1.5-electron S2s

measurements.what: Stress tests on statistically independent samples
measurements.result: Relaxed exclusion cuts (mean single-photon rate 6 times higher, single-electron rate 3 times higher), AmLi neutron calibration (high isolated-S2 rate) and physical-drift-time events failing shape cuts: all pass; pulse-based cuts reject 95% of accidentals

measurements.result: Isolated S1: interactions in charge-insensitive regions, Cherenkov and fluorescent light in detector materials, dark-noise pile-up; isolated S2: radioactivity or electron emission from cathode or gate, interactions in the gas or in the liquid above the gate, drifting electrons trapped on impurities and released with O(100 ms) delay

measurements.what: 'Stingers'
measurements.result: Small S1-like signals attributed to misalignment of the gate and anode grids; raised at the LIDINE 2026 round table, with no published description.

setups.key_results: LZ predicts accidentals from data alone: 1.2 ± 0.3 (WS2022), 2.8 ± 0.6 (WS2024, 4.2 t yr) and 6.6 ± 0.3 events (WS2025 low-mass search, 5.7 t yr, 1.15 per tonne-year), the last being about 30% of the final 19-event sample and the dominant background below 9 GeV. Random pairing under-predicts the lowest S1/S2 bins; pairing within the same photon/electron-rate environment restores agreement with the unphysical-drift-time sideband (p = 0.38, 0.48, 0.28). The WS2025 letter defers details to 'an upcoming publication', which had not appeared on arXiv as of 18 Nov 2026.

pile-up of single photons into S1s and of single electrons into S2s
charge-insensitive regions, grid emission, PMT dark counts (named sources)

setups.institute: INFN Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS)
setups.location_note: Detector underground at LNGS. Approximate position of the underground laboratory, beside the A24 motorway tunnel a few km from the surface laboratory at Assergi.
setups.years_active: 2020– (science runs SR0-SR2, May 2021 – March 2025, analysed so far)
setups.description: Dual-phase TPC with 5.9 t of active liquid xenon (8.5 t total) in a 1.33 m diameter, 1.49 m tall cylinder, read by 494 3-inch R11410-21 PMTs, with a 23 V/cm drift field, 2.9 kV/cm extraction field and a 2.2 ms maximum drift time. The long drift window and the lower extraction efficiency make the isolated-S2 rate about ten times that of XENON1T, so accidental coincidences dominate the low-energy searches. They are handled with a data-driven simulation that pairs measured isolated S1s and S2s (axidence), cuts on the time and position 'shadow' of preceding large S2s (S2pre/dt_pre), and S1 and S2 boosted decision trees; the S2-only search adds a conditional normalising flow for delayed electrons and a cathode BDT. Gate and anode carry perpendicular support wires that emit single electrons locally.

measurements.what: Isolated-pulse rates before mitigation in the 2-hit ⁸B search
measurements.result: Isolated S1 about 15 Hz, isolated S2 about 0.15 Hz; with a 2.25 ms maximum drift time this gives about 400 accidental events per day

measurements.what: Isolated-pulse rates after all cuts (SR0 / SR1), ⁸B search, 3.51 t yr
measurements.result: S1 2.3 / 2.2 Hz; S2 18 / 26 mHz; shadow cuts remove more than 80% of isolated S1s and position-time cuts more than 50% of isolated S2s at about 96% signal acceptance; overall cut acceptance 75% (2-hit) and 85% (3-hit)

measurements.what: Accidental expectation and validation, ⁸B search SR0+SR1
measurements.result: 7.5 ± 0.7 (SR0) and 17.8 ± 1.0 (SR1) events out of 26.4 (+1.4/-1.3) total background, 37 observed; sideband goodness-of-fit p = 0.16; uncertainty 9.0% / 5.8%; S2 BDT rejects about 90% of accidentals at 80% signal acceptance

measurements.what: Isolated-pulse and accidental rates in the three-run ⁸B analysis (6.77 t yr), SR0 / SR1 / SR2
measurements.result: S1 2.3 / 2.2 / 1.7 Hz; S2 16.6 / 21.5 / 17.7 mHz; accidentals after all selections 0.80 / 0.99 / 0.60 µHz; SR2 rates about 20% lower through better peak classification

measurements.what: Accidental expectation in the three-run ⁸B analysis as shown at IDM 2026
measurements.result: 40.2 ± 1.4 accidentals out of 42.1 (+1.9/-1.7) expected background; 62 events observed; 3.3 sigma

measurements.what: Isolated-pulse rates and accidental expectation in the SR0 WIMP search (3-fold S1)
measurements.result: S1 1.5 Hz, S2 80 mHz, event window 2.2 ms; 4.3 ± 0.9 accidentals expected; validation on ³⁷Ar data: 731.6 predicted vs 733 observed, 2D p = 0.61; 30% rate uncertainty assigned

measurements.what: Definition of the shadow cuts
measurements.result: Veto within one drift time of S1 > 10³ PE or S2 > 10⁴ PE; beyond that, time shadow S2prev/dt_prev < 0.038 PE/ns (96% acceptance) and a half-Cauchy position shadow (about 97% acceptance)

measurements.what: Photoionisation strength (electrons within one drift time after an S2, relative to that S2)
measurements.result: Rose by about an order of magnitude between SR0 and SR1 after a maintenance period and fell again in SR2 after a hydrocarbon filter was installed; the S2 threshold of the SR1 WIMP search was raised from 200 to 320 PE because of the higher accidental rate

measurements.what: Delayed lone PMT hits after large S2s (fit beyond 2.2 ms over a 150 s window, power law with exponential cut-off)
measurements.result: Constant term 1.8 kHz, exponent k = -0.65, cut-off τ = 0.28 s, amplitude 0.065 PE/Hz; the 7 brightest PMTs take 40% of an S2's light but only 6% of the lone hits, so quartz-window photoluminescence is not the sole mechanism; PMT dark counts (<50 Hz per PMT) are too few

measurements.what: Complete S2-only background model, 7.83 t yr over 579 days (S2 of about 3-16 electrons)
measurements.result: Components: cathode (²¹⁰Pb chain), delayed electrons up to about 1 s after large S2s, accidental electrons (pile-up of randomly emitted single electrons), ⁸B. SR0 (1.50 t yr): cathode 480 ± 70, delayed electrons 1.3 ± 0.5, accidental electrons 97 ± 17, ⁸B 21 ± 5, total 600 ± 80, observed 583. Cathode BDT rejects about 70% at 80% signal; delayed-electron BDT (with normalising-flow score) rejects about 95% at 90% signal; hit-pattern model rejects about 75% of accidental electrons at 99% signal

measurements.what: Single-to-five-electron search (SR0 subsets of 14.3 and 16.5 days)
measurements.result: Few-electron background persisting O(100) ms after interactions is mitigated with spatial and temporal vetoes and a 39.5 cm radius cut; single-electron gain 31.15 PE

measurements.what: Wall charge-insensitive volume
measurements.result: Stated at the LIDINE 2026 round table to be under study through S1 position reconstruction in an S1-only analysis; no result yet

setups.key_results: Before mitigation XENONnT sees about 15 Hz of isolated S1s and 0.15 Hz of isolated S2s, i.e. about 400 accidental pairs per day in a 2.2 ms window; shadow cuts bring these to 2.3 Hz and 18-26 mHz, and the BDTs remove about 90% of what remains, leaving 7.5 + 17.8 accidental events in the 3.51 t yr ⁸B search and 40.2 ± 1.4 in the 6.77 t yr one, still the dominant background. The S2-only search (7.83 t yr) has the first complete background model, dominated by cathode events and accidental single-electron pile-up, with delayed electrons suppressed to the event level. The delayed lone-hit rate after large S2s follows a power law with a 0.28 s cut-off and does not track the S2 hit pattern, which points away from quartz-window photoluminescence alone and motivates the material photoluminescence measurements at Nikhef; the mechanism is stated to be not understood.
mechanisms: delayed single photons (lone hits) after large S2s piling up into isolated S1s
photoluminescence of detector materials (PTFE contaminants, solder flux, quartz windows) - candidate
delayed electrons after large S2s (release from impurities; possibly triggered by delayed photons)
photoionisation of impurities in bulk and on surfaces within one drift time; strength varied by an order of magnitude between runs
single-electron emission and bursts near the perpendicular electrode wires and a hot spot
cathode events with charge loss (S2-only)
charge-insensitive volume at the walls (under study)
PMT dark counts (bounded, minor)

setups.institute: China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL-II), hall B2
setups.location_note: Detector in hall B2 of CJPL-II under Jinping mountain; approximate position (CJPL site). The collaboration is led from Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
setups.years_active: 2021– (commissioning-run paper 2021; Run0 and Run1 analysed, 259 days of ionisation-only data)
setups.description: Dual-phase TPC with a 3.7 t liquid-xenon sensitive target read by two arrays of Hamamatsu R11410-23 PMTs. Events are built in a fixed 2 ms window; isolated S1s and S2s found in data are scrambled and stitched at waveform level to model accidentals, and a BDT separates them from ⁸B signals. An 'afterglow' veto removes time (and, for S2-only data, an 80 mm cylinder) after signals above 10,000 PE to suppress delayed electrons. The ionisation-only ('US2') channel reaches 0.33 keV nuclear-recoil threshold and is limited by cathode events and by pile-up of delayed electrons, historically called the 'micro-discharging' (MD) background.

measurements.what: Isolated-pulse rates in the 1.54 t yr WIMP search (Run0 / Run1), loose cuts, 2 ms window
measurements.result: Isolated S1 13.3 / 14.4 Hz; isolated S2 0.125 / 0.146 Hz; accidental expectation 5.6 ± 1.7 and 7.9 ± 2.4 events

measurements.what: Accidental background in the ⁸B analysis, paired channel (1.20 t yr)
measurements.result: AC 1.08 ± 0.28 and 0.07 ± 0.02 (Run0, 2-hit and 3-hit), 1.15 ± 0.35 and 0.24 ± 0.08 (Run1); total paired background 2.8 ± 0.5, 3 observed; 15% model uncertainty from off-window and 1-hit sidebands; BDT takes the off-window prediction from 180 ± 27 to 0.9 ± 0.2 (Run0)

measurements.result: Exposure loss 23% (34%) for paired and 26% (33%) for US2 data in Run0 (Run1); 29.1 days of US2 data dropped for abnormal rates

measurements.result: 251 ± 32 background events expected, 332 observed; cathode events largest, MD second

measurements.result: Expected: cathode 204 ± 32, MD (delayed-electron pile-up) 45 ± 5, ⁸B 43 ± 7; paired channel: AC 2.5 ± 0.5, ⁸B 3.4 ± 0.6

measurements.what: First ⁸B search (commissioning data): accidental model and BDT
measurements.result: About 1000 S2s per day in 65-300 PE; a random waveform holds on average 6.3 single-hit S1-like signals (mostly dark noise); BDT removes 98% (2-hit) and 96% (3-hit) of accidentals; diffusion cut suppresses AC by about a factor 8

measurements.what: Delayed electrons after large signals vs detector conditions
measurements.result: Strong correlation in both distance and time with the large signal; rate is higher at higher electron lifetime, for longer drift time of the large signal, and for larger S2 (qualitative, plots only); a deadtime cut helps but delayed electrons still dominate small S2-only events and are negligible above 5 electrons

measurements.what: Electrode events
measurements.result: Gate events removed by S2 width; cathode events cannot be fully removed; selection efficiency 0 below 20 µs drift and about 5% above 800 µs for 5-65 electrons (waveform simulation); cathode S2s are smaller than gate S2s at similar S1, with a preliminary electron-loss model at the cathode wires

setups.key_results: PandaX-4T sees about 13-14 Hz of isolated S1s and 0.13-0.15 Hz of isolated S2s under loose cuts, close to the XENONnT values, and controls accidentals with waveform-level scrambling, sidebands and a BDT (about 1 accidental event per run in the ⁸B paired sample). In the ionisation-only channel the backgrounds are cathode events and pile-up of delayed electrons. The delayed-electron rate rises with electron lifetime, with the parent's drift time and with S2 size; the first of these is opposite to the purity trend reported by XENON1T and LUX and is not explained in the talk.

cathode and gate electrode events (cathode radioactivity with electron loss at the wires)
dark-noise pile-up into isolated S1s
electrode and PMT discharges (periods with abnormal isolated-S1 rate removed)

setups.name: DarkSide-20k (design)
setups.institute: INFN Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS)
setups.location_note: Detector under construction underground at LNGS (Hall C); approximate position of the underground halls. The cited accidental-coincidence modelling was presented by authors at Astrocent (Warsaw) and APC (Paris).
setups.years_active: under construction; operation expected from 2027 (2024 collaboration paper)
setups.description: Dual-phase argon TPC with 50 t of underground argon (20 t fiducial), SiPM photon detection units, a Gd-loaded acrylic vessel, ESR reflector and TPB wavelength shifter, one extraction grid and transparent Clevios-coated electrodes instead of wire anode/gate grids, and no PTFE. For the high-mass WIMP search with S1 + S2 the accidental-coincidence model is built from simulation because there are no data yet. Two populations are simulated: S1-only events from alpha decays in or on the ESR reflector and TPB at the walls, and 'unresolved' events near the liquid surface where the field above the grid is about 17 times the drift field so that S1 and S2 merge into one S2-like pulse.

measurements.what: Identification of the dominant isolated-S1 source in DS-20k.
measurements.result: Alpha-decay scintillation in the ESR reflector (dominant; Rn-daughter deposition) and in TPB, plus charge lost to the walls through field non-uniformity; mitigated by S1 pulse-shape cuts ('LongS1tail' cut, used in DS-50)

measurements.what: Identification of the dominant isolated-S2 source in DS-20k.
measurements.result: Unresolved S1+S2 from low-energy ER decays (β/γ from U/Th, ⁴⁰K, ⁶⁰Co, ¹³⁷Cs) near the liquid surface; field above the extraction grid ≈ 17× the drift field

measurements.what: Simulation-weighted combinatorial AC model: every simulated surface alpha is paired with every simulated unresolved event, by isotope and location; each pair is weighted by measured activities, simulated efficiencies, maximum drift time and livetime; the rate is the sum of weights surviving all cuts.
measurements.result: Prediction quoted per 10 years of exposure; no rate given in the public slides; to be checked against the sideband once data exist

measurements.what: Risk ranking of xenon-TPC isolated-S2 sources for DS-20k.
measurements.result: Grid electron emission 'middle' (not observed in DS-50, no guarantee in DS-20k); delayed electrons after S2s 'low (too small)' for the NR region of interest

measurements.what: Underlying TPB measurement used for the surface-alpha cut: long-lived TPB scintillation under alpha excitation.
measurements.result: TPB component with ~ms lifetime, different in size for alpha, beta and VUV excitation; surface-background suppression by more than 10³

setups.key_results: For DarkSide-20k the expected accidental-coincidence background pairs surface-alpha S1-only events on ESR/TPB walls with unresolved S1+S2 events from the high-field region above the grid. Its rate is predicted from a simulation-weighted combinatorial model rather than from data, and the model can only be validated on sidebands after the detector starts. In the collaboration's assessment, electron trains and grid emission, which dominate in xenon, have no direct analogue in the DS-20k nuclear-recoil region of interest.

setups.institute: Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics SB RAS and Novosibirsk State University
setups.years_active: 2020–2023 (slow-component programme)
setups.description: Two-phase argon detector with an electroluminescence (EL) gap read out by cryogenic PMTs and SiPMs, with and without wavelength shifter, later coupled to a THGEM. The group systematically measured the pulse shape of the S2 (EL) signal and discovered unusual slow components that they interpret as delayed electrons temporarily trapped in the gas phase.

measurements.what: Electroluminescence pulse shapes at reduced fields of 3–9 Td.
measurements.result: A fast component plus two slow components with time constants of about 5 µs and about 40–50 µs, whose contribution and time constants increase with field.

measurements.what: Threshold and temperature dependence of the slow components.
measurements.result: They appear above 4.8 ± 0.2 Td independent of gas density; their contribution decreases with temperature and nearly vanishes at room temperature.

measurements.what: THGEM coupled to the electroluminescence gap.
measurements.result: A similar slow component is seen in the THGEM electroluminescence signal and, in multiplication mode, directly in the charge signal, showing that the slow component is carried by delayed electrons.

setups.key_results: The slow S2 components cannot be explained by thermionic emission from the liquid or by triplet excimer emission; the authors attribute them to drifting electrons trapped on metastable negative argon ions in the gas and released with microsecond delays. They note that such delayed electrons add to single-electron noise in argon dark-matter detectors.

setups.name: Freiburg single-phase liquid-only xenon TPC (XeBRA platform)
setups.institute: University of Freiburg (Schumann group)
setups.description: Small single-phase liquid-only xenon TPC with light readout above and below a cylindrical target, in which the S2 is produced by proportional scintillation in the liquid around 10 µm anode wires. It was built to demonstrate a design without a liquid-gas interface, which removes delayed electron extraction at the surface as a source of lone S2s. The published abstract reports gain and transport results only; the link to accidental coincidences is the design motivation of the single-phase concept.

measurements.what: Charge gain with the anode 4.4 kV above the gate, measured with ⁸³ᵐKr lines at 32.1 and 9.4 keV.
measurements.result: Up to (1.9 ± 0.3) PE per electron, i.e. (29 ± 6) photons per ionisation electron.

measurements.what: Electron drift velocity and longitudinal diffusion at 470 V/cm.
measurements.result: Consistent with literature.

measurements.what: S2 width versus drift.
measurements.result: Dominated by electron diffusion, approaching the xenon de-excitation time for short drifts.

setups.key_results: Demonstrates S2 generation in liquid xenon without a gas phase, a hardware route to eliminating surface-trapped delayed electrons. No delayed-electron rate measurement is reported in the abstract.
mechanisms: delayed extraction at the liquid surface (avoided by design)
single-phase proportional scintillation

references.title: Proportional scintillation in liquid xenon: demonstration in a single-phase liquid-only time projection chamber
Proportional scintillation in liquid xenon: demonstration in a single-phase liquid-only time projection chamber
Prospects of charge signal analyses in liquid xenon TPCs with proportional scintillation in the liquid phase

caveats: No delayed-electron measurement is published from this setup; its relevance is the interface-free design.

setups.name: XENONnT R11410-21 PMT test facilities (Zurich, Stockholm, MPIK): light emission and afterpulses
setups.institute: University of Zurich; Stockholm University; Max-Planck-Institut für Kernphysik Heidelberg
setups.location_note: Multi-site: Zurich, Stockholm, Heidelberg; pin at Zurich.
setups.medium: Xe (liquid and gas); Ar gas at MPIK
setups.description: Three PMT test stands used for the XENONnT qualification campaign: an upgraded xenon cryostat for 10 PMTs in Zurich, a new xenon cryostat for 14 PMTs in Stockholm, and a room-temperature Faraday-cage setup plus a gaseous-argon cryostat at MPIK. New tests were developed specifically for PMT light emission and for afterpulse growth from vacuum leaks, both observed in XENON1T.

measurements.what: Qualification of R11410-21 PMTs in cryogenic xenon.
measurements.result: 368 tubes tested; 26 rejected.

measurements.what: Micro light emission at 1.5 kV.
measurements.result: Most tubes emit at a few Hz to tens of Hz; five tubes with kHz-level emission and six with intermittent emission were rejected (11 tubes, 3.0%).

measurements.what: Afterpulses from vacuum degradation (nitrogen, xenon or argon afterpulse lines).
measurements.result: 15 tubes (4.1%) rejected; tubes with argon afterpulse rate above 0.01% had a 17% failure rate versus 1% below.

measurements.what: Stress tests at about 5×10⁵ PE/s, and good PMTs facing leaky PMTs.
measurements.result: Light emission triggered in five cases; good PMTs facing leaky ones saw small (<5 PE) signals attributed to photons emitted during afterpulsing.

setups.key_results: PMT light emission, whose random coincidence with single-electron signals was a significant accidental-coincidence background in XENON1T, can be screened before installation. Afterpulse monitoring identifies leaky tubes that also emit light seen by neighbouring PMTs.
mechanisms: PMT light emission
PMT afterpulses
PMT dark counts
lone-hit pile-up into fake S1

references.title: Improved quality tests of R11410-21 photomultiplier tubes for the XENONnT experiment

caveats: Multi-site entry: the pin marks Zurich only.

setups.name: MEPhI R11410-20 PMT light-emission test (RED-100 PMT qualification)
setups.institute: National Research Nuclear University MEPhI
setups.medium: vacuum-tube bench test (room temperature down to -60 °C)
setups.description: Bench test of Hamamatsu R11410-20 photomultipliers in which a noisy tube is viewed by a second PMT to look for emitted photons. It is distinct from the RED-100 TPC itself and concerns the photosensors used in liquid-xenon detectors.

measurements.what: Search for photons emitted by high-voltage-biased R11410-20 tubes, viewed by a second PMT.
measurements.result: Tubes with dark count rates above 10 kHz emit single photons.

measurements.what: Temperature range of the effect.
measurements.result: Seen in a few units at room temperature and down to -60 °C.

setups.key_results: First report that noisy R11410 PMTs emit light, i.e. a dark-count excess in one tube can inject single photons into the rest of the array. The authors flag it for rare-event searches with small energy deposits in massive xenon detectors.
mechanisms: PMT light emission
PMT dark counts
lone-hit pile-up into fake S1

references.title: Observation of light emission from Hamamatsu R11410-20 photomultiplier tubes

caveats: The effect was seen in a few units only.
The institute affiliation is inferred from the author list.

setups.name: Zurich SiPM characterisation and Xurich II SiPM TPC
setups.institute: University of Zurich (Baudis group)
setups.description: Characterisation of Hamamatsu VUV4 6×6 mm² SiPMs between 110 and 300 K in nitrogen gas and in liquid xenon, followed by Xurich II, the first dual-phase xenon TPC with a SiPM top array (16 SiPMs plus a bottom PMT). The 2018 paper motivates the dark-count measurement by the need to minimise accidental coincidences at low thresholds; it does not compute an accidental rate.

measurements.what: SiPM dark count rate at 172 K, 0.5 PE threshold and 5.6 V overvoltage.
measurements.result: 0.82 Hz/mm², about 80 times the 0.01 Hz/mm² of cryogenic PMTs.

measurements.what: Optical crosstalk probability and gain at 172 K and 5.6 V overvoltage.
measurements.result: Crosstalk 4.1%; gain 1.5×10⁶.

measurements.what: Xurich II: dual-phase TPC with SiPM readout, calibrated with ⁸³ᵐKr and ³⁷Ar.
measurements.result: Calibration down to 2.82 keV; horizontal position resolution about 1.5 mm.

setups.key_results: VUV4 SiPM dark counts at liquid-xenon temperature remain nearly two orders of magnitude above PMTs, which the authors identify as the obstacle for low-threshold S1 coincidence requirements.
mechanisms: SiPM dark counts
SiPM correlated noise / crosstalk
lone-hit pile-up into fake S1

references.title: Characterisation of Silicon Photomultipliers for Liquid Xenon Detectors
The first dual-phase xenon TPC equipped with silicon photomultipliers and characterisation with 37Ar

caveats: The papers characterise the sensors and the TPC; no accidental-coincidence rate is computed.

setups.name: TRIUMF MIEL setup: SiPM secondary photon emission (external crosstalk)
setups.institute: TRIUMF (Retière group)
setups.description: Custom apparatus (MIEL) that measures the spectrum and yield of secondary photons emitted by SiPM avalanches when the device is stimulated by laser light near operating voltage. It was built in the nEXO context but quantifies the external-crosstalk photons that create correlated few-photon coincidences in any SiPM-instrumented noble-liquid detector.

measurements.what: Secondary photon yield per avalanche at 4 V overvoltage, Hamamatsu VUV4.
measurements.result: 40 ± 9 photons per avalanche.

measurements.what: Secondary photon yield per avalanche at 4 V overvoltage, FBK VUV-HD3.
measurements.result: 61 ± 11 photons per avalanche.

measurements.what: Temperature dependence of the secondary photon yield between 86 K and 293 K.
measurements.result: No significant dependence.

setups.key_results: Tens of secondary photons are emitted per SiPM avalanche, so dark counts in one device can trigger others across the detector.
mechanisms: SiPM external crosstalk
SiPM dark counts
correlated lone hits piling up into fake S1

references.title: Stimulated Secondary Emission of Single Photon Avalanche Diodes

caveats: Built in the nEXO context; the relevance to dark-matter accidental coincidences is indirect.
The institute affiliation is inferred from the author list.

setups.name: TPB delayed-emission measurement (Segreto)
setups.institute: Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP), Instituto de Física Gleb Wataghin
setups.location_note: Pin at the author's institute; the measurement site is not stated in the paper (the TPB film was produced at LNGS).
setups.medium: Ar (liquid-argon cell data) and vacuum (alpha/beta excitation of TPB film)
setups.description: Analysis of a 0.7 l TPB-coated liquid-argon cell viewed by one PMT, combined with a vacuum-chamber test in which a TPB film is excited by alpha and beta sources. It shows that tetraphenyl butadiene re-emits part of the 127 nm argon light with long delays.

measurements.what: Time structure of the TPB response to 127 nm argon scintillation light.
measurements.result: Instantaneous component 60 ± 1%, intermediate 49 ± 1 ns (30 ± 1%), long 3550 ± 500 ns (8 ± 1%), and a 309 ± 10 ns component (2 ± 1%).

measurements.what: Delayed fraction of the wavelength-shifted light.
measurements.result: About 40% is delayed; the delayed emission is non-exponential and attributed to triplet-triplet interaction.

setups.key_results: TPB is not a prompt wavelength shifter: a microsecond-scale delayed component follows every argon scintillation pulse. This is a material-fluorescence source of late single photons in argon TPCs using TPB.
mechanisms: wavelength-shifter delayed fluorescence
delayed single photons after S1/S2
material photoluminescence

references.title: Evidence of delayed light emission of TetraPhenyl Butadiene excited by liquid Argon scintillation light

caveats: The measurement site is not stated in the paper; the pin marks the author's institute.
The paper does not discuss accidental coincidences.
